overview:
Datadog's Palo Alto Networks Firewall Log integration allows customers to ingest, parse, and analyze Palo Alto Networks firewall logs. This log integration relies on the HTTPS log templating and forwarding capability provided by PAN OS, the operating system that runs in Palo Alto firewalls. PAN-OS allows customers to forward threat, traffic, authentication, and other important log events.

### Key use cases
#### Respond to high severity threat events
Firewall threat logs provide context on threats detected by a firewall, which can be filtered and analyzed by severity, type, origin IPs/countries, and more.

#### Make informed decisions on Firewall deployment
Firewall traffic logs can be used to measure the traffic and sessions passing through a firewall and also gives you the ability to monitor for anomalous throughput across firewall deployment.

#### Monitor authentication anomalies
Firewall authentication logs provide detailed information on users as they authenticate with Palo Alto Networks firewall. These logs can be used to monitor anomalous spikes in authentication traffic from specific protocols, users, locations, and more.

**Minimum Agent version:** 7.31.1
setup:
### Log collection

 1. [Install the Datadog Agent][1] on a machine that is reachable by the firewall and can connect to the internet. Confirm that log collection is enabled. To enable log collection, change `logs_enabled: false` to `logs_enabled: true` in your Agent's main configuration file (datadog.yaml). See the [Host Agent Log collection documentation][10] for more information and examples.
 2. In PanOS, Select Device >> Server Profiles >> Syslog , add a name for the server profile. Follow the Syslog log forwarding [configuration steps][2]. Same steps listed below.
 3. Click Add and provide the following details of the server:
 	* Name of the server
 	* IP address of the machine with datadog agent
 	* Transport as TCP
 	* Port as 10518 and format as BSD
 4. Copy and configure custom log format for the required log type. The formats below are mappings from the formats listed in [the Palo Alto Networks Syslog Field Descriptions docs][8].

 5. Click OK, this creates a syslog server profile.
 6. Click on the Objects tab, this opens the log forwarding profile screen.
 7. Create log forwarding profile by providing the name, log type and syslog profile
 8. Create a pan.firewall.d/conf.yaml file at the root of the [Agent's configuration directory][3] with the below content.

     ```yaml
     logs:
     - type: tcp
       port: 10518
       service: "firewall"
       source: "pan.firewall"
     ```
 9. [Restart Agent][4].

metrics.name: pan_firewall.api.authentication.status
metrics.description: Whether the API rejected the credentials (1 = invalid credentials, 0 = OK).

metrics.name: pan_firewall.bgp.peer.connections.dropped
metrics.description: BGP connections dropped. Sent only by the Advanced Routing Engine.

metrics.name: pan_firewall.bgp.peer.connections.established
metrics.description: BGP connections established. Sent only by the Advanced Routing Engine.

metrics.name: pan_firewall.bgp.peer.prefix_limit
metrics.description: Configured maximum prefixes. The Advanced Routing Engine reports a limit per address family (`afi_safi`); the legacy routing engine reports one limit per peer.

metrics.name: pan_firewall.bgp.peer.prefix_limit.utilization
metrics.description: Accepted prefixes as a percentage of the configured limit.

metrics.name: pan_firewall.bgp.peer.prefixes.incoming.rejected
metrics.description: Prefixes rejected. Not sent by the Advanced Routing Engine.

metrics.name: pan_firewall.bgp.peer.prefixes.incoming.total
metrics.description: Prefixes received. Not sent by the Advanced Routing Engine.

metrics.name: pan_firewall.bgp.peer.prefixes.outgoing.total
metrics.description: Prefixes to send. Not sent by the Advanced Routing Engine.

metrics.name: pan_firewall.bgp.peer.restart
metrics.description: Whether the BGP peer came up in the last 30 minutes (1 = came up, 0 = did not come up).

metrics.name: pan_firewall.bgp.peer.status
metrics.description: Whether the BGP peer is established (1 = established, 0 = not established).

metrics.name: pan_firewall.can_connect
metrics.description: Whether the firewall API responded during the last check run (1 = responded, 0 = did not respond).

metrics.name: pan_firewall.counter.global
metrics.description: Increase of the PAN-OS global counter, tagged by counter name, category, and aspect.

metrics.name: pan_firewall.disk.used_pct
metrics.description: Percentage of file system space used, reported every 30 minutes. Not sent for the `none`, `tmpfs`, or `cgroup_root` file systems.

metrics.name: pan_firewall.dropped_packets
metrics.description: Dropped packets by aspect. Known aspects report 0 when they have no drops. Other aspects, such as `mgmt`, are reported when present.

metrics.name: pan_firewall.interface.flow_state
metrics.description: Packets dropped by flow state check.

metrics.name: pan_firewall.interface.speed
metrics.description: Interface speed, reported every 30 minutes. Not sent when the speed is `ukn` or `[n/a]`.

metrics.name: pan_firewall.ipsec.tunnel.rx.bytes
metrics.description: Bytes received through the IPsec tunnel.

metrics.name: pan_firewall.ipsec.tunnel.rx.packets
metrics.description: Packets received through the IPsec tunnel.

metrics.name: pan_firewall.ipsec.tunnel.state
metrics.description: IPsec tunnel state (0 = inactive, 1 = active, 2 = initializing). Unknown states are not sent.

metrics.name: pan_firewall.ipsec.tunnel.tx.bytes
metrics.description: Bytes sent through the IPsec tunnel.

metrics.name: pan_firewall.ipsec.tunnel.tx.packets
metrics.description: Packets sent through the IPsec tunnel.

metrics.name: pan_firewall.license.days_left
metrics.description: Days until the license expires, reported every 24 hours. Not sent for perpetual licenses.

metrics.name: pan_firewall.license.expired
metrics.description: Whether the license has expired (1 = expired, 0 = not expired), reported every 24 hours.

metrics.name: pan_firewall.mgmt.memory.available
metrics.description: Memory available for new processes without swapping.

metrics.name: pan_firewall.mgmt.memory.used_pct
metrics.description: Percentage of management-plane memory in use.

metrics.name: pan_firewall.mgmt.swap.used_pct
metrics.description: Percentage of management-plane swap in use.

metrics.name: pan_firewall.ospf.neighbor.state_changes
metrics.description: OSPF neighbor state changes. Sent only by the Advanced Routing Engine.

metrics.name: pan_firewall.ospf.neighbor.status
metrics.description: Whether the OSPF neighbor is in the `full` state (1 = full, 0 = not full).

metrics.name: pan_firewall.panorama.can_connect
metrics.description: Whether the Panorama discovery call succeeded (1 = succeeded, 0 = failed).

metrics.name: pan_firewall.power.alarm.high
metrics.description: Whether the power sensor is in alarm above the maximum (1 = in alarm, 0 = not in alarm).

metrics.name: pan_firewall.power.alarm.low
metrics.description: Whether the power sensor is in alarm below the minimum (1 = in alarm, 0 = not in alarm).

metrics.name: pan_firewall.report.top.bytes
metrics.description: Traffic in the last 24 hours, reported every 30 minutes.

metrics.name: pan_firewall.report.top.bytes_per_session
metrics.description: Average traffic per session, reported every 30 minutes.

metrics.name: pan_firewall.report.top.sessions
metrics.description: Sessions in the last 24 hours, reported every 30 minutes.

metrics.name: pan_firewall.temperature.alarm
metrics.description: Whether the temperature sensor is in alarm (1 = in alarm, 0 = not in alarm).
